name: Two competing drafts for blind persona review

context.target_audience: Support operations leaders managing a growing email queue

evidence.text: RelayDesk drafts suggested replies from approved knowledge articles and leaves the final send to an agent.
Every suggestion records which approved knowledge article it used.

claim_contract.text: RelayDesk drafts suggested support replies from approved knowledge articles for an agent to review.
RelayDesk records the approved knowledge article behind each suggestion.
RelayDesk helps support teams keep response work moving while agents retain the final send decision.

buyer_personas: A support operations lead accountable for response quality and queue health
A skeptical customer experience director whose last automation pilot produced unreliable answers

email.subject: A reply draft with its source attached
email.preview_text: Agents can inspect the approved article before they send
email.body:
A faster first reply is useful only if the agent can tell where the answer came from. Otherwise review becomes a second research job.

RelayDesk drafts a suggested reply from approved knowledge articles and records the article behind the suggestion. The final send stays with the agent who owns the conversation.

That gives reviewers something concrete to inspect: the proposed answer beside the source it used. They can correct the wording without hunting through a separate knowledge base first.

Use one recurring email question as the test and compare the suggestion with the answer an experienced agent would trust.

email.subject: Keep the support queue moving
email.preview_text: A simpler way to help agents answer routine questions
email.body:
A growing support queue puts pressure on every part of the team. Routine questions compete with the conversations that genuinely need judgment and care.

RelayDesk helps support teams keep response work moving while agents retain the final send decision. It offers a practical way to organise the work around answers the team already uses.

That can give people more room to focus on customers and fewer routine tasks to manage. The workflow stays familiar while the first step becomes easier to handle.

If a smoother support process is worth exploring, look at the workflow and decide whether it fits the way the team prefers to work.
